title: Britpop
tagline: Guitar pop with a distinctly British voice and a taste for big choruses.
summary: Britpop became a prominent British guitar-music movement in the 1990s. Its bands drew from earlier UK pop and rock while writing about everyday life, place, and identity in a direct, often witty style. The movement brought guitar bands back to the center of popular music and created a recognizable era of competing scenes and anthemic singles.

pillars.name: Blur
pillars.why: Blur used character-driven lyrics and shifting pop arrangements to become one of Britpop's defining bands.

pillars.name: Oasis
pillars.why: Oasis paired direct songwriting with large choruses and a classic-rock scale that defined the movement's mainstream reach.

pillars.name: Pulp
pillars.why: Pulp's observational lyrics and carefully built songs offered a distinctive, socially attentive take on Britpop.
